title.zh: 卷三 本紀第三: 憲宗
title.raw: 卷三 本紀第三: 憲宗 Volume 3 Annals 3: Xianzong

sentences.zh: 憲宗桓肅皇帝，諱蒙哥，睿宗拖雷之長子也。

translations.literal: Xianzong, the Emperor Huansu — taboo name Möngke — was the eldest son of Ruizong Tolui.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, styled the Emperor Huansu, bore the personal name Möngke and was the eldest son of Ruizong Tolui.

sentences.zh: 母曰莊聖太后，怯烈氏，諱唆魯禾帖尼。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng of the Kereit clan, personal name Sorghaghtani Beki.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Dowager Zhuang Sheng of the Kereit, Sorghaghtani Beki.

sentences.zh: 歲戊辰，十二月三日生帝。

translations.literal: In the year wuchen, on the third day of the twelfth month, the Emperor was born.
translations.idiomatic: He was born on the third day of the twelfth month of the wuchen year.

sentences.zh: 時有黃忽答部知天象者，言帝后必大貴，故以蒙哥為名。

translations.literal: At that time a diviner of the Yellow Quda tribe who read the heavens said the child would surely attain the greatest eminence, and so he was named Möngke.
translations.idiomatic: A stargazer of the Yellow Quda tribe declared that the child was destined for greatness, and for that reason he was named Möngke.

sentences.zh: 蒙哥，華言長子也。

translations.literal: Möngke, in Chinese speech, means "eldest son."
translations.idiomatic: Möngke, in Chinese, means "eldest son."

sentences.zh: 太宗在潛邸，養以為子，屬昂灰皇后撫育之。

translations.literal: When Ögedei was still heir apparent, he raised the boy as his own son and entrusted his upbringing to Empress Anggwi.
translations.idiomatic: While Ögedei was still heir apparent, he took the boy as a son and placed him under the care of Empress Anggwi.

sentences.zh: 既長，為娶火魯剌部女火裏差為妃，分之部民。

translations.literal: When he had grown, a wife was taken for him — Huolicha, daughter of the Qorolas tribe — and a share of the tribe's households was allotted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was given Huolicha, a daughter of the Qorolas, as his consort, together with a portion of that tribe's households.

sentences.zh: 及睿宗薨，乃命歸籓邸。

translations.literal: When Ruizong died, he was ordered to return to his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Ruizong's death he was ordered back to his own princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 從征伐，屢立奇功。

translations.literal: He followed on campaigns and repeatedly won extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign after campaign he won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 嘗攻欽察部，其酋八赤蠻逃於海島。

translations.literal: Once, attacking the Qipchaq, their chieftain Bachman fled to an island in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Once, in an attack on the Qipchaq, their chieftain Bachman escaped to a sea island.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，亟進師，至其地，適大風刮海水去，其淺可渡。

translations.literal: Hearing of it, the Emperor hurried the army forward. When they reached the place, a great wind happened to blow the seawater back, leaving the shallows passable on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard this, he pressed the army forward at once. At the site a great wind drove the sea back, and the shallows became fordable.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「此天開道與我也。

translations.literal: The Emperor said in delight: "Heaven has opened a road for me."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, he said, "Heaven has cleared a path for me."

sentences.zh: 」遂進屠其眾，擒八赤蠻，命之跪，八赤蠻曰：「我為一國主，豈苟求生？

translations.literal: He then pressed forward, slaughtered Bachman's force, and captured Bachman. He ordered Bachman to kneel. Bachman said: "I am sovereign of a realm — would I beg merely to live?"
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, cut down Bachman's followers, and seized Bachman himself. Ordered to kneel, Bachman replied, "I am king of a nation — shall I grovel merely to survive?"

sentences.zh: 且身非駝，何以跪人為？

translations.literal: Besides, my body is not a camel's — why should I kneel before another man?"
translations.idiomatic: And I am no camel — why should I kneel to another man?"

sentences.zh: 」乃命囚之。

translations.literal: He was therefore ordered imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 八赤蠻謂守者曰：「我之竄入於海，與魚何異，然終見擒，天也。

translations.literal: Bachman said to his guards: "When I hid myself in the sea I was no different from a fish, yet in the end I was captured — it was Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Bachman told his guards, "When I fled into the sea I was little better than a fish, yet I was taken in the end — Heaven willed it.

sentences.zh: 今水回期且至，軍宜早還。

translations.literal: The tide will soon return; the army ought to withdraw at once."
translations.idiomatic: The returning tide is nearly upon us. The army should withdraw while it still can."

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，即班師，而水已至，後軍有浮渡者。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he at once ordered the army to withdraw; the water had already risen, and in the rear some men were carried off while crossing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard him and ordered an immediate withdrawal. The water was already rising; in the rear some men were swept away as they crossed.

sentences.zh: 復與諸王拔都征斡羅思部，至也烈贊城，躬自搏戰，破之。

translations.literal: Again, with Prince Batu, he campaigned against the Rus' and came to Yaroslavl, where he fought hand to hand himself and broke the city.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again with Prince Batu against the Rus', reached Yaroslavl, fought in the front ranks himself, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 歲戊申，定宗崩，朝廷久未立君，中外洶洶，咸屬意於帝，而覬覦者眾，議未決。

translations.literal: In the year wushen, Güyük died. The court long went without a ruler; inside and outside there was turmoil, and all looked to the Emperor — yet many also coveted the throne, and no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: In the wushen year Güyük died. For a long time the throne stood empty; alarm spread through court and camp alike, and though many looked to Möngke, others coveted the succession and no agreement could be reached.

sentences.zh: 諸王拔都木哥、阿裏不哥、唆亦哥禿、塔察兒，大將兀良合台、速你帶、帖木迭兒、也速不花，咸會于阿剌脫忽剌兀之地，拔都首建議推戴。

translations.literal: The princes Batu, Möngke, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar; the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa — all met at Alagh Tagh, and Batu was the first to propose installing him.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Batu, Möngke, Ariq Böke, Sögtü, and Tachar, together with the generals Uriyangqadai, Sübetei, Temüder, and Yesu Buqa, assembled at Alagh Tagh, where Batu first moved to have him raised up.

sentences.zh: 時定宗皇后海迷失所遣使者八剌在坐，曰：「昔太宗命以皇孫失烈門為嗣，諸王百官皆與聞之。

translations.literal: At that time Bal, an envoy sent by Güyük's empress Oghul Qaimish, was present and said: "Formerly Ögedei commanded that the imperial grandson Shiremün be his successor, and all the princes and officials heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Bal, an envoy of Güyük's empress Oghul Qaimish, was present and said, "Ögedei once commanded that his grandson Shiremün succeed him, and every prince and official heard the order.

sentences.zh: 今失烈門故在，而議欲他屬，將置之何地耶？

translations.literal: Shiremün is still alive, yet you now wish to choose another — where, then, is he to be placed?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiremün is still alive. If you mean to set the succession elsewhere, what place is left for him?"

sentences.zh: 」木哥曰：「太宗有命，誰敢違之。

translations.literal: Möngke said: "Ögedei gave the command — who would dare disobey it?
translations.idiomatic: Möngke answered, "Who would dare defy Ögedei's command?

sentences.zh: 然前議立定宗，由皇后脫列忽乃與汝輩為之，是則違太宗之命者，汝等也，今尚誰咎耶？

translations.literal: Yet when Güyük was chosen before, it was Empress Töregene and you who did it — so it was you who broke Ögedei's command. Whom do you blame now?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Güyük was chosen, it was Empress Töregene and your party who did it. You were the ones who broke Ögedei's command — whom do you blame now?"

sentences.zh: 」八剌語塞。

translations.literal: Bal was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Bal had no reply.

sentences.zh: 兀良合台曰：「蒙哥聰明睿知，人咸知之，拔都之議良是。

translations.literal: Uriyangqadai said: "Möngke is clear-minded and wise — all men know it. Batu's proposal is sound."
translations.idiomatic: Uriyangqadai said, "Möngke's intelligence is known to all. Batu's proposal is right."

sentences.zh: 」拔都即申令於眾，眾悉應之，議遂定。

translations.literal: Batu then proclaimed the decision before the assembly; all assented, and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Batu announced the decision to the assembly. All agreed, and the choice was settled.

sentences.zh: 元年辛亥夏六月，西方諸王別兒哥、脫哈帖木兒，東方諸王也古、脫忽、亦孫哥、按只帶、塔察兒、別裏古帶，西方諸大將班裏赤等，東方諸大將也速不花等，復大會於闊帖兀阿闌之地，共推帝即皇帝位於斡難河。

translations.literal: In the first year, xinhai, summer, sixth month: the western princes Berke and Toghtamur; the eastern princes Yeke, Toghu, Yissüngge, Ajai, Tachar, and Belgütei; the western generals, including Barchin; and the eastern generals, including Yesu Buqa, met again at Kötö'ü Adal and together raised the Emperor to the throne on the Onon River.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year (xinhai), in the sixth month of summer, the western princes Berke and Toghtamur, the eastern princes Yeke, Toghu, Yissüngge, Ajai, Tachar, and Belgütei, the western generals led by Barchin, and the eastern generals led by Yesu Buqa met again at Kötö'ü Adal and together enthroned him on the Onon River.

sentences.zh: 失烈門及諸弟腦忽等心不能平，有後言。

translations.literal: Shiremün and his younger brothers, including Naqu, were inwardly discontented and spoke afterward against the decision.
translations.idiomatic: Shiremün and his brothers, among them Naqu, nursed their resentment and murmured against the choice.

sentences.zh: 帝遣諸王旭烈與忙可撒兒帥兵覘之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Prince Hulagu and Mangqasar at the head of troops to watch them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Prince Hulagu and Mangqasar with troops to keep watch over them.

sentences.zh: 諸王也速忙可、不裏、火者等後期不至，遣不憐吉率兵備之。

translations.literal: The princes Yesü Möngke, Buri, and Qoja and others arrived late and did not come; Bulghu was sent with troops to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Yesü Möngke, Buri, Qoja, and others failed to appear on time; Bulghu was dispatched with troops to stand ready against them.

sentences.zh: 遂改更庶政：命皇弟忽必烈領治蒙古、漢地民戶；

translations.literal: He then reformed the government at large: he ordered his imperial brother Kublai to administer the Mongol and Han households;
translations.idiomatic: He then reorganized the government: his brother Kublai was put in charge of Mongol and Han households;

sentences.zh: 遣塔兒、斡魯不、察乞剌、賽典赤、趙璧等詣燕京，撫諭軍民；

translations.literal: Taer, Orbu, Chaqil, Saiyid Ajall, Zhao Bi, and others were sent to Yanjing to reassure soldiers and civilians;
translations.idiomatic: Taer, Orbu, Chaqil, Saiyid Ajall, Zhao Bi, and others were sent to Yanjing to reassure the army and people;

sentences.zh: 以忙哥撒兒為斷事官；

translations.literal: Mangqasar was made chief judge;
translations.idiomatic: Mangqasar was appointed chief judge;

sentences.zh: 以孛魯合掌宣發號令、朝覲貢獻及內外聞奏諸事；

translations.literal: Bolghu was charged with proclaiming edicts, receiving tribute at court, and all internal and external memorials;
translations.idiomatic: Bolghu was charged with issuing orders, receiving tribute and petitions, and handling all reports from within and without;

sentences.zh: 以晃兀兒留守和林宮闕、帑藏，阿藍答兒副之；

translations.literal: Qongqor was left to guard the Karakorum palace and treasury, with Arghun Aqa as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Qongqor was left to guard the Karakorum palace and treasury, assisted by Arghun Aqa;

sentences.zh: 以牙剌瓦赤、不只兒、斡魯不、睹答兒等充燕京等處行尚書省事，賽典赤、匿昝馬丁佐之；

translations.literal: Yarlaghchi, Bujir, Orbu, Tuda'er, and others were appointed to the Yanjing Branch Secretariat, assisted by Saiyid Ajall and Nizam al-Din;
translations.idiomatic: Yarlaghchi, Bujir, Orbu, Tuda'er, and others were made heads of the Yanjing Branch Secretariat, with Saiyid Ajall and Nizam al-Din as deputies;

sentences.zh: 以訥懷、塔剌海、麻速忽等充別失八里等處行尚書省事，暗都剌兀尊、阿合馬、也的沙佐之；

translations.literal: Negü, Talqai, Mas'ud, and others were appointed to the Beshbaligh Branch Secretariat, assisted by Endureltü, Ahmad, and Yazid;
translations.idiomatic: Negü, Talqai, Mas'ud, and others were appointed to the Beshbaligh Branch Secretariat, with Endureltü, Ahmad, and Yazid assisting;

sentences.zh: 以阿兒渾充阿毋河等處行尚書省事，法合魯丁、匿只馬丁佐之；

translations.literal: Arghun was appointed to the Amu Darya Branch Secretariat, assisted by Fakhr al-Din and Nizam al-Din;
translations.idiomatic: Arghun was put in charge of the Amu Darya Branch Secretariat, with Fakhr al-Din and Nizam al-Din as deputies;

sentences.zh: 以茶寒、葉了幹統兩淮等處蒙古、漢軍，以帶答兒統四川等處蒙古、漢軍，以和裏統土蕃等處蒙古、漢軍，皆仍前征進；

translations.literal: Chaghan and Yol Qan were put in command of the Mongol and Han armies of the Two Huai region; Taidar of those in Sichuan; and Qoridai of those in Tibet — all continuing the prior advance;
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan and Yol Qan were given command of the Mongol and Han forces in the Two Huai; Taidar of those in Sichuan; and Qoridai of those in Tibet — each continuing the campaigns already under way;

sentences.zh: 以僧海雲掌釋教事，以道士李真常掌道教事。

translations.literal: the monk Haiyun was put in charge of Buddhist affairs, and the Daoist Li Zhenchang of Daoist affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the monk Haiyun was placed over Buddhist affairs and the Daoist Li Zhenchang over Daoist affairs.

sentences.zh: 葉孫脫、按只、暢吉、爪難、合答曲憐、阿裏出及剛疙疸、阿散、忽都魯等，務持兩端，坐誘諸王為亂，並伏誅。

translations.literal: Yesünto, Ajai, Changgi, Jaqan, Qadaqutling, Ariq, and others — together with Gang Qudan, Asan, Qutluq, and the rest — kept to both sides and were convicted of inciting the princes to rebellion; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yesünto, Ajai, Changgi, Jaqan, Qadaqutling, Ariq, Gang Qudan, Asan, Qutluq, and others who had straddled both factions were found guilty of inciting princes to revolt and were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 遂頒便益事宜于國中：凡朝廷及諸王濫發牌印、詔旨、宣命，盡收之；

translations.literal: Beneficial measures were then promulgated throughout the realm: all seals, edicts, and commissions improperly issued by the court or by princes were recalled;
translations.idiomatic: Useful reforms were then proclaimed throughout the realm: every seal, edict, and commission wrongly issued by court or princes was recalled;

sentences.zh: 諸王馳驛，許乘三馬，遠行亦不過四；

translations.literal: princes on courier service were permitted three horses, and even on long journeys no more than four;
translations.idiomatic: princes using the post roads were limited to three horses, and to four even on long journeys;

sentences.zh: 諸王不得擅招民戶；

translations.literal: princes might not privately recruit households;
translations.idiomatic: princes were forbidden to recruit households on their own authority;

sentences.zh: 諸官屬不得以朝覲為名賦斂民財；

translations.literal: officials might not levy the people's wealth under the pretext of coming to court;
translations.idiomatic: officials might not extort the people under the pretense of attending court;

sentences.zh: 民糧遠輸者，許於近倉輸之。

translations.literal: where grain taxes had to be transported far, delivery at a nearer granary was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: where grain had to be transported a great distance, payment into a nearer granary was allowed.

sentences.zh: 罷築和林城役千五百人。

translations.literal: The corvée building Karakorum was halted, releasing fifteen hundred laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Work on Karakorum was stopped, freeing fifteen hundred laborers.

sentences.zh: 冬，以宴只吉帶違命，遣合丹誅之，仍籍其家。

translations.literal: In winter, because Yeshügü had disobeyed orders, Qadan was sent to execute him and his household goods were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yeshügü was executed by Qadan for disobedience, and his property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 二年壬子春正月，幸失灰之地，遣乞都不花攻末來吉兒都怯寨。

translations.literal: In the second year, renzi, spring, first month, the Emperor visited Shihui; Qutuq Buqa was sent to attack the fortress of Mergen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (renzi), in the first month of spring, he visited Shihui and sent Qutuq Buqa to attack the fortress of Mergen.

sentences.zh: 皇太后崩。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 夏，駐蹕和林。

translations.literal: In summer he halted at Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he halted at Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 分遷諸王於各所：各丹于別石八里地，蔑裏于葉兒的石河，海都於海押立地，別兒哥于曲兒只地，脫脫于葉密立地，蒙哥都及太宗皇后乞裏吉忽帖尼於擴端所居地之西。

translations.literal: The princes were dispersed to their posts: Kadan to Beshbaligh; Möri to the Irtysh River; Kaidu to the Aybagh; Berke to Quriltai; Tögtö to Yemek; and Möngke Quduq, together with Ögedei's empress Qurijin Khatun, to the west of Kuoto.
translations.idiomatic: The princes were sent to their assigned territories: Kadan to Beshbaligh, Möri to the Irtysh River, Kaidu to Aybagh, Berke to Quriltai, Tögtö to Yemek, and Möngke Quduq with Ögedei's empress Qurijin Khatun to the west of Kuoto.

sentences.zh: 仍乙太宗諸后妃家貲分賜親王。

translations.literal: The goods of Ögedei's consorts and concubines were again divided and bestowed upon the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei's consorts and concubines had their goods divided anew and distributed among the princes.

sentences.zh: 定宗後及失烈門母以厭禳事覺，並賜死，謫失烈門、也速、孛裏等於沒脫赤之地，禁錮和只、納忽、也孫脫等於軍營。

translations.literal: Güyük's empress and Shiremün's mother were discovered in sorcery and both were granted death; Shiremün, Yesü, and Buri were banished to Motuo and placed under restraint, and Qoju, Naqu, and Yesünto were confined in the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Güyük's empress and Shiremün's mother were found guilty of sorcery and put to death; Shiremün, Yesü, and Buri were exiled to Motuo under guard, while Qoju, Naqu, and Yesünto were held in the camps.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，命忽必烈征大理，諸王禿兒花、撒立征身毒，怯的不花征沒裏奚，旭烈征西域素丹諸國。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, Kublai was ordered to campaign against Dali; the princes Törel and Sali against Sind; Qutuq Buqa against the Merkit; and Hulagu against the sultanates of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Kublai was ordered against Dali; Princes Törel and Sali against Sind; Qutuq Buqa against the Merkit; and Hulagu against the sultanates of the west.

sentences.zh: 詔諭宋荊南、襄陽、樊城、均州諸守將，使求附。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to the Song commanders at Jingnan, Xiangyang, Fancheng, and Junzhou, urging them to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were sent to the Song garrison commanders at Jingnan, Xiangyang, Fancheng, and Junzhou inviting them to submit.

sentences.zh: 八月，忽必烈次臨洮，命總帥汪田哥以城利州聞，欲為取蜀之計。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Kublai halted at Lintao and ordered the commander Wang Tiange to hold Lizhou, intending this as the opening move for taking Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Kublai halted at Lintao and ordered the commander Wang Tiange to hold Lizhou as the first step toward taking Shu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，命諸王也古征高麗。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the prince Yeke was ordered to campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Prince Yeke was ordered to campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕月帖古忽闌之地。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at Yedige Qulan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor halted at Yedige Qulan.

sentences.zh: 時帝因獵墜馬傷臂，不視朝百餘日。

translations.literal: At that time, while hunting, the Emperor fell from his horse and injured his arm; for more than a hundred days he did not hold court.
translations.idiomatic: While hunting he fell from his horse and injured his arm, and for more than a hundred days he did not hold audience.

sentences.zh: 三年癸丑春正月，汪田哥修治利州，且屯田，蜀人莫敢侵軼。

translations.literal: In the third year, guichou, spring, first month, Wang Tiange repaired Lizhou and opened fields for garrison farming; the people of Shu did not dare encroach.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (guichou), in the first month of spring, Wang Tiange repaired Lizhou and opened garrison farms; the people of Shu did not dare raid across the border.

sentences.zh: 帝獵於怯蹇義罕之地。

translations.literal: The Emperor hunted at Qeqen Yeqan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hunted at Qeqen Yeqan.

sentences.zh: 諸王也古以怨襲諸王塔剌兒營。

translations.literal: Prince Yeke, nursing a grievance, attacked Prince Tachar's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yeke, nursing a grievance, raided Prince Tachar's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝遂會諸王于斡難河北，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor then summoned the princes north of the Onon and lavished gifts upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then assembled the princes north of the Onon and rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 罷也古征高麗兵，以劄剌兒帶為征東元帥。

translations.literal: Yeke's army against Goryeo was withdrawn, and Jachar was made commander of the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yeke's Goryeo expedition was recalled, and Jachar was made commander of the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 遣必闍別兒哥括斡羅思戶口。

translations.literal: Bijä Beg was sent to register the households of the Rus'.
translations.idiomatic: Bijä Beg was sent to register Rus' households.

sentences.zh: 三月，大兵攻海州，戍將王國昌逆戰於城下，敗之，獲都統一人。

translations.literal: In the third month the great army attacked Haizhou; the garrison commander Wang Guochang met them beneath the walls and was defeated; one Song commander was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the main army attacked Haizhou. The garrison commander Wang Guochang gave battle beneath the walls and was defeated; one Song commander was taken.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，命諸王旭烈兀及兀良合台等帥師征西域哈裏發八哈塔等國。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer, Prince Hulagu and Uriyangqadai and others were ordered to lead armies against the caliphates of Baghdad and elsewhere in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of summer Prince Hulagu, Uriyangqadai, and others were ordered west against the caliphates of Baghdad and the surrounding lands.

sentences.zh: 又命塔塔兒帶撒裏、土魯花等征欣都思、怯失迷兒等國。

translations.literal: Tatar was also ordered, with Sali, Tuluhua, and others, to campaign against Hindustan, Kashmir, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Tatar was likewise ordered, with Sali, Tuluhua, and others, against Hindustan, Kashmir, and neighboring realms.

sentences.zh: 帝幸火兒忽納要不兒之地。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Qorqonaq Buir.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor visited Qorqonaq Buir.

sentences.zh: 諸王拔都遣脫必察詣行在，乞買珠銀萬錠，以千錠授之，仍詔諭之曰：「太祖、太宗之財，若此費用，何以給諸王之賜！

translations.literal: Prince Batu sent Töbchä to the imperial camp, requesting ten thousand ingots of pearls and silver; one thousand ingots were granted, and an edict admonished him: "If the wealth of Taizu and Ögedei is spent in this way, how will the princes' allotments be met!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Batu sent Töbchä to the imperial camp to request ten thousand ingots of pearls and silver. One thousand were granted, with an admonition: "If Taizu and Ögedei's treasure is squandered thus, how are the princes' yearly grants to be paid?

sentences.zh: 王宜詳審之。

translations.literal: The prince ought to consider this carefully.
translations.idiomatic: You should weigh the matter carefully.

sentences.zh: 此銀就充今後歲賜之數。

translations.literal: Let this silver count toward your yearly grant from this time forward."
translations.idiomatic: Consider this silver as part of your yearly allotment from now on."

sentences.zh: 」秋，幸軍腦兒。

translations.literal: In autumn he visited Jünna'ur.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he visited Jünna'ur.

sentences.zh: 以忙可撒兒為萬戶，哈丹為劄魯花赤。

translations.literal: Mangqasar was made a commander of ten thousand; Qadan was made jarquchi.
translations.idiomatic: Mangqasar was made commander of ten thousand, and Qadan jarquchi.

sentences.zh: 九月，忽必烈次忒剌地，分兵三道以進。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Kublai halted at Tere and divided his army into three columns to advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Kublai halted at Tere and divided his force into three columns for the advance.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，大理平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Dali was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Dali was pacified in the twelfth month of winter.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕汪吉地。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at Wangi.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor halted at Wangi.

sentences.zh: 命宗王耶虎與洪福源同領軍征高麗，攻拔禾山、東州、春州、三角山、楊根、天龍等城。

translations.literal: Prince Yehu and Hong Wonyuan were ordered jointly to lead troops against Goryeo and took the cities of Hesam, Dongju, Chunju, Samgaksan, Yanggeun, and Cheonnyong, among others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yehu and Hong Wonyuan were ordered to lead a joint expedition against Goryeo and captured Hesam, Dongju, Chunju, Samgaksan, Yanggeun, Cheonnyong, and other cities.

sentences.zh: 是歲，斷事官忙哥撒兒卒。

translations.literal: That year the chief judge Mangqasar died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the chief judge Mangqasar died.

sentences.zh: 四年甲寅春，帝獵於怯蹇義罕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, jiayin, spring, the Emperor hunted at Qeqen Yeqan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (jiayin), in spring, the Emperor hunted at Qeqen Yeqan.

sentences.zh: 夏，幸月兒滅怯土之地。

translations.literal: In summer he visited Yürümiq Tütu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer he visited Yürümiq Tütu.

sentences.zh: 遣劄剌亦兒部人火兒赤征高麗。

translations.literal: Qorichi of the Jadran tribe was sent to campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Qorichi of the Jadran was sent against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，詔官吏之赴朝理算錢糧者，許自首不公，仍禁以後浮費。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn an edict declared that officials coming to court to settle accounts might confess prior injustice and would still be pardoned, while future waste was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn an edict allowed officials arriving for court audits to confess past irregularities and still be pardoned, while forbidding further waste.

sentences.zh: 冬，大獵於也滅幹哈裏義海之地。

translations.literal: In winter a great hunt was held at the Yemüqan Qorqai Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In winter a great hunt was held at the Yemüqan Qorqai Sea.

sentences.zh: 忽必烈還自大理，留兀良合台攻諸夷之未附者，入覲於獵所。

translations.literal: Kublai returned from Dali, leaving Uriyangqadai to attack the unsubdued tribes and coming himself to the hunt to pay homage.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai returned from Dali, left Uriyangqadai to subdue the tribes still holding out, and came to the hunt to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 是歲，會諸王於顆顆腦兒之西，乃祭天於日月山。

translations.literal: That year the princes were assembled west of Gegen Na'ur, and Heaven was worshipped at Sun-and-Moon Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That year the princes were assembled west of Gegen Na'ur, and sacrifice was offered to Heaven at Sun-and-Moon Mountain.

sentences.zh: 初籍新軍。

translations.literal: New troops were first registered.
translations.idiomatic: New troops were registered for the first time.

sentences.zh: 帝謂大臣，求可以慎固封守、閑於將略者。

translations.literal: The Emperor told his ministers that he sought men skilled in holding the frontiers firm and versed in military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked his ministers to find men capable of securing the borders and skilled in command.

sentences.zh: 擢史樞征行萬戶，配以真定、相、衛、懷、孟諸軍，駐唐、鄧。

translations.literal: Shi Shu was promoted to campaigning commander of ten thousand, given the armies of Zhending, Xiang, Wei, Huai, and Meng, and stationed at Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shu was promoted to campaigning commander of ten thousand, given the forces of Zhending, Xiang, Wei, Huai, and Meng, and posted at Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 張柔移鎮亳州。

translations.literal: Zhang Rou was transferred to garrison Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou was transferred to garrison Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 權萬戶史權屯鄧州。

translations.literal: Acting commander of ten thousand Shi Quan was stationed at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Acting commander Shi Quan was posted at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 張柔遣張信將八漢軍戍潁州。

translations.literal: Zhang Rou sent Zhang Xin with the Eight Han Armies to garrison Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou sent Zhang Xin with the Eight Han Armies to garrison Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王安國將四千戶渡漢南，深入而還。

translations.literal: Wang Anguo led four thousand households across the Han southward, raided deep into enemy territory, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anguo led four thousand households south across the Han, raided deep into Song territory, and returned.

sentences.zh: 張柔以連歲勤兵，兩淮艱於糧運，奏據亳之利。

translations.literal: Because Zhang Rou had kept his army in the field year after year and grain transport in the Two Huai was difficult, he memorialized to hold Bozhou for its advantages.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou, having campaigned year after year while grain transport in the Two Huai grew ever harder, memorialized to hold Bozhou for its logistical advantages.

sentences.zh: 詔柔率山前八軍，城而戍之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Rou to lead the Eight Armies south of the mountains, build a city, and garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Rou to lead the Eight Armies south of the mountains, build a fortified city, and garrison it.

sentences.zh: 柔又以渦水北隘淺不可舟，軍既病涉，曹、濮、魏、博粟皆不至，乃築甬路自亳抵汴，堤百二十里，流深而不能築，復為橋十五，或廣八十尺，橫以二堡戍之。

translations.literal: Rou also found the Guo River north of the city too narrow and shallow for boats; with the army suffering from the crossings, grain from Cao, Pu, Wei, and Bo failed to arrive. He therefore built a raised road from Bozhou to Bian, a dike one hundred twenty li long; where the current ran too deep to dike, he built fifteen bridges, some eighty feet wide, and guarded them with two forts.
translations.idiomatic: Rou found the Guo River north of the city too shallow for boats; the army suffered on the crossings, and grain from Cao, Pu, Wei, and Bo never arrived. He built a raised causeway from Bozhou to Bian, a hundred and twenty li of embankment; where the water ran too deep to embank, he threw fifteen bridges across it, some eighty feet wide, each flanked by a fort.

sentences.zh: 均州總管孫嗣遣人齎蠟書降，且乞援，史權以精甲備宋人之要，遂援嗣而來。

translations.literal: Sun Si, administrator of Junzhou, sent men bearing a letter of surrender in wax and begged for relief; Shi Quan, with picked armor, guarded against a Song ambush and went to bring Si in.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Si, prefect of Junzhou, sent envoys with a sealed letter of surrender and a plea for aid; Shi Quan, with elite troops, guarded against Song interception and went to bring him in.

sentences.zh: 其後驍將鐘顯、王梅、杜柔、袁師信各帥所部來降。

translations.literal: Thereafter the valiant generals Zhong Xian, Wang Mei, Du Rou, and Yuan Shixin each led their units to come over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the fierce commanders Zhong Xian, Wang Mei, Du Rou, and Yuan Shixin each brought their forces in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 五年乙卯春，詔征逋欠錢谷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, yimao, an edict ordered the collection of arrears in money and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year (yimao), an edict went out to levy all overdue taxes and grain.

sentences.zh: 夏，帝幸月兒滅怯土。

translations.literal: In summer the Emperor visited Yier-mieqietu.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Emperor traveled to Yier-mieqietu.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，張柔會大帥于符離。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Zhang Rou joined the supreme commander at Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn Zhang Rou rendezvoused with the supreme commander at Fuli.

sentences.zh: 以百丈口為宋往來之道，可容萬艘，遂築甬路，自亳而南六十餘里，中為橫江堡。

translations.literal: Because Baizhangkou was the route by which the Song came and went and could accommodate ten thousand vessels, they built a causeway more than sixty li south from Bo, with a fort across the river in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhangkou lay on the Song traffic route and could shelter ten thousand boats, so they raised a causeway south from Bo for more than sixty li, placing a river-crossing fort midway.

sentences.zh: 又以路東六十里皆水，可致宋舟，乃立柵水中，惟密置偵邏于所達之路，由是鹿邑、寧陵、考、柘、楚丘、南頓無宋患，陳、蔡、潁、息皆通矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, for sixty li east of the route all was water through which Song boats could be brought up; they therefore set palisades in the water and only secretly posted scouts on the paths that led there. Thus Luyi, Ningling, Kao, Zhe, Qiuqiu, and Nandun were free of Song trouble, and Chen, Cai, Ying, and Xi were all linked.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty li east of the road was open water where Song vessels could be brought up, so they drove stakes into the shallows and posted scouts only along the hidden approaches. Luyi, Ningling, Kao, Zhe, Qiuqiu, and Nandun were soon clear of Song raids, and Chen, Cai, Ying, and Xi lay open once more.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改命劄剌與洪福源同征高麗。

translations.literal: That year Qarachar was reassigned to campaign against Goryeo jointly with Hong Wonyu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qarachar was ordered to join Hong Wonyu in the campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 後此又連三歲，攻拔其光州、安城、忠州、玄風、珍原、甲向、玉果等城。

translations.literal: Over the three years that followed they stormed and took Guangzhou, Ancheng, Chungju, Hyeonpung, Jinwon, Gaphyang, Okgwa, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: For the next three years they pressed the attack, seizing Guangzhou, Ancheng, Chungju, Hyeonpung, Jinwon, Gaphyang, Okgwa, and other strongholds.

sentences.zh: 六年丙辰春，大風起北方，砂礫飛揚，白日晦冥。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, bingchen, a great wind rose from the north; sand and gravel flew about, and the bright day turned dark.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year (bingchen) a gale blew out of the north, sand and gravel whirling until broad daylight went dim.

sentences.zh: 帝會諸王、百官於欲兒陌哥都之地，設宴六十餘日，賜金帛有差，仍定擬諸王歲賜錢谷。

translations.literal: The Emperor assembled princes and officials at Yier-mogedu, feasted for more than sixty days, granted gold and silk in varying measure, and fixed the annual allotments of money and grain for the princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gathered princes and officials at Yier-mogedu, feasted for more than sixty days, distributed gold and silk in graded gifts, and set the princes' yearly grants of money and grain.

sentences.zh: 忽必烈遣沒兒合石詣行在所，奏請續簽內郡漢軍，從之。

translations.literal: Kublai sent Mör-gechi to the imperial camp to petition for conscripting more Han troops from the interior circuits; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai dispatched Mör-gechi to the mobile court to ask for further conscription of Han troops from the interior circuits, and the petition was approved.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，駐蹕於塔密兒。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he halted at Tamir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month he encamped at Tamir.

sentences.zh: 五月，幸昔剌兀魯朵。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he visited Sire Ordo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he went to Sire Ordo.

sentences.zh: 六月，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Venus appeared in the daytime sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Venus was seen in daylight.

sentences.zh: 幸亦兒阿答。

translations.literal: He visited Yier-ada.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Yier-ada.

sentences.zh: 諸王亦孫哥、駙馬也速兒等請伐宋。

translations.literal: The princes Yisun and the imperial son-in-law Yesür and others petitioned to attack the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yisun, the imperial son-in-law Yesür, and others asked leave to march against the Song.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以宋人違命囚使，會議伐之。

translations.literal: The Emperor too, because the Song had defied his orders and imprisoned his envoys, convened a council to discuss campaigning against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, angered that the Song had defied his commands and held his envoys captive, called a council to plan war against them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，命諸王各還所部以居。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he ordered the princes each to return to their appanages and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he sent each prince back to his own domain to take up residence.

sentences.zh: 諸王塔察兒、駙馬帖裏垓軍過東平諸處，掠民羊豕，帝聞，遣使問罪，由是諸軍無犯者。

translations.literal: When the army of Prince Tachar and the imperial son-in-law Teligai passed through Dongping and neighboring districts, it plundered the people's sheep and pigs. On hearing of this the Emperor sent envoys to demand an accounting, whereupon no army dared offend again.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tachar and the imperial son-in-law Teligai led their troops through Dongping and the surrounding districts, seizing the people's sheep and swine. When word reached the Emperor he sent envoys to demand an accounting, and from then on no army dared molest the populace.

sentences.zh: 是歲，波麗國王細嵯甫、雲南酋長摩合羅嵯及素丹諸國來覲。

translations.literal: That year the King of Poli, Xicuofu; the Yunnan chieftain Moheluo-cuo; and envoys from the Sultan states came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Xicuofu of Poli, the Yunnan chieftain Moheluo-cuo, and envoys from the Sultan lands all came to court.

sentences.zh: 兀良合台討白蠻等，克之；

translations.literal: Uryankhadai suppressed the White Man tribes and others, defeating them;
translations.idiomatic: Uryankhadai marched against the White Man and other tribes and broke them;

sentences.zh: 遂自昔八兒地還至重慶府，敗宋將張都統。

translations.literal: he then returned from Sibar territory to Chongqing Prefecture and routed the Song commander Zhang Dutong.
translations.idiomatic: then, coming back from Sibar, he reached Chongqing Prefecture and routed the Song commander Zhang Dutong.

sentences.zh: 賜金縷織文衣一襲、銀五十兩、彩帛萬二百匹，以賚軍士。

translations.literal: He was granted one gold-thread embroidered robe, fifty taels of silver, and ten thousand two hundred bolts of colored silk to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He received one gold-thread embroidered robe, fifty taels of silver, and ten thousand two hundred bolts of colored silk with which to reward his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 冬，帝駐蹕阿塔哈帖乞兒蠻。

translations.literal: In winter the Emperor halted at Ataha-teqirmen.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Emperor encamped at Ataha-teqirmen.

sentences.zh: 以阿木河回回降民分賜諸王百官。

translations.literal: The Muslim populace that had submitted on the Amu River was divided and granted to princes and officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Muslim subjects who had surrendered along the Amu River were divided up and granted to princes and officials.

sentences.zh: 七年丁巳春，幸忽闌也兒吉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, dingsi, he visited Hulan-yierji.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year (dingsi) he went to Hulan-yierji.

sentences.zh: 詔諸王出師征宋。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the princes to take the field against the Song.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded the princes to take the field against the Song.

sentences.zh: 乞都不花等討末來吉兒都怯寨，平之。

translations.literal: Qutuq-buqa and others suppressed the Melaiji'r-duqie stockade and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Qutuq-buqa and his commanders reduced the Melaiji'r-duqie stockade and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，謁太祖行宮，祭旗鼓，復會于怯魯連之地，還幸月兒滅怯土。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer he visited the mobile palace of Taizu, sacrificed to the banners and drums, assembled again at Kerulen, and returned to Yier-mieqietu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth summer month he visited Taizu's traveling palace, offered sacrifice to the banners and drums, met again at Kerulen, and returned to Yier-mieqietu.

sentences.zh: 秋，駐蹕於軍腦兒，釃馬乳祭天。

translations.literal: In autumn he halted at Junnao'er and poured fermented mare's milk in sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he encamped at Junnao'er and poured fermented mare's milk in sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 九月，出師南征。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the army marched south on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army set out on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 以駙馬剌真之子乞為達魯花赤，鎮守斡羅思，仍賜馬三百、羊五千。

translations.literal: Qachi, son of the imperial son-in-law Racheen, was appointed darughachi to garrison Rus', and was further granted three hundred horses and five thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Qachi, son of the imperial son-in-law Racheen, was made darughachi to hold Rus', and was given three hundred horses and five thousand sheep besides.

sentences.zh: 回鶻獻水精盆、珍珠傘等物，可直銀三萬餘錠。

translations.literal: The Uighurs presented a crystal basin, a pearl umbrella, and other objects worth more than thirty thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs offered a crystal basin, a pearl umbrella, and other treasures worth more than thirty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「方今百姓疲弊，所急者錢爾，朕獨有此何為？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "The people are exhausted now; what they need is money. Of what use is it for me alone to possess these things?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The people are worn out; what they need is money. What good does it do for me alone to keep such things?

sentences.zh: 」卻之。

translations.literal: " He refused them.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent them back.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤以為言，帝稍償其直，且禁其勿復有所獻。

translations.literal: Sayyid Ajall spoke on their behalf; the Emperor partially compensated their value and forbade them from presenting gifts again.
translations.idiomatic: Sayyid Ajall pleaded their case; the Emperor paid part of the value and forbade further tribute of that kind.

sentences.zh: 宗王塔察兒率諸軍南征，圍樊城，霖雨連月，乃班師。

translations.literal: Prince Tachar led the armies south, besieged Fancheng, but after rains persisted for months, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tachar led the southern armies against Fancheng, but month after month of rain forced him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 元帥卜鄰吉軍自鄧州略地，遂渡漢江。

translations.literal: The marshal Qorichin's army raided from Dengzhou and crossed the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Qorichin's force raided out of Dengzhou and crossed the Han River.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，兀良合台伐交趾，敗之，入其國。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Uryankhadai attacked Annam, defeated it, and entered the country.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh winter month Uryankhadai invaded Annam, broke its armies, and entered the realm.

sentences.zh: 安南主陳日煚竄海島，遂班師。

translations.literal: King Trần Thái Tông of Annam fled to a sea island, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: King Trần Thái Tông of Annam fled to an offshore island, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遣阿藍答兒、脫因、囊加台等詣陝西等處理算錢谷。

translations.literal: Arghun Aqa, To'in, Nangatai, and others were dispatched to Shaanxi and other regions to audit taxes and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Arghun Aqa, To'in, Nangatai, and others were sent to Shaanxi and neighboring circuits to settle accounts of taxes and grain.

sentences.zh: 冬，帝度漠南，至於玉龍棧。

translations.literal: In winter the Emperor crossed south of the desert as far as Yulongzhan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Emperor crossed south of the desert and reached Yulongzhan.

sentences.zh: 忽必烈及諸王阿裏不哥、八里土、出木哈兒、玉龍塔失、昔烈吉、公主脫滅幹等來迎，大燕，既而各遣歸所部。

translations.literal: Kublai and the princes Ariq Böke, Bari-tu, Chumqar, Yulutas, Siregi, and Princess Tuomiegan came to meet him; a great banquet was held, and afterward each was sent back to his appanage.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai and the princes Ariq Böke, Bari-tu, Chumqar, Yulutas, and Siregi, together with Princess Tuomiegan, came out to meet him. A great feast was held, and afterward each was sent home to his domain.

sentences.zh: 八年戊午春正月朔，幸也裏本朵哈之地，受朝賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of spring in the eighth year, wuwu, he visited Yilibenduoha and received court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day in the spring of the eighth year (wuwu) he went to Yilibenduoha and received the court's congratulations.

sentences.zh: 二月，陳日煚傳國于長子光昺。

translations.literal: In the second month Trần Thái Tông passed the realm to his eldest son Quang Hựu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Trần Thái Tông abdicated in favor of his eldest son Quang Hựu.

sentences.zh: 光昺遣婿與其國人以方物來見，兀良合台送詣行在所。

translations.literal: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with his countrymen bearing tribute to audience; Uryankhadai escorted them to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Quang Hựu sent his son-in-law with Annamese envoys bearing tribute; Uryankhadai escorted them to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 諸王旭烈兀討回回哈裏發，平之，禽其王，遣使來獻捷。

translations.literal: Prince Hulagu suppressed the Muslim caliphate, pacified it, captured its king, and sent envoys to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hulagu crushed the Muslim caliphate, brought the land to order, took its king prisoner, and sent envoys bearing news of victory.

sentences.zh: 帝獵於也裏海牙之地。

translations.literal: The Emperor hunted at Yilihaiya.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hunted at Yilihaiya.

sentences.zh: 師南征，次於河。

translations.literal: The army marched south and halted at the river.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army advanced and encamped on the river.

sentences.zh: 適冰合，以土覆之而渡。

translations.literal: The ice had just formed; they covered it with earth and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: The river had just frozen over; they spread earth atop the ice and crossed.

sentences.zh: 帝自將伐宋，由西蜀以入。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally commanded the campaign against the Song, entering through western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took personal command of the war against the Song, entering by way of western Shu.

sentences.zh: 命張柔從忽必烈征鄂，趨杭州。

translations.literal: Zhang Rou was ordered to follow Kublai in the campaign against Ezhou, pressing toward Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou was ordered to march with Kublai against Ezhou and drive toward Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 命塔察攻荊山，分宋兵力。

translations.literal: Tachar was ordered to attack Jingshan, dividing Song forces.
translations.idiomatic: Tachar was ordered to strike Jingshan and split the Song armies.

sentences.zh: 宋四川制置使蒲澤之攻成都，紐鄰率師與戰，敗之；

translations.literal: Song Sichuan commissioner Pu Zezhi attacked Chengdu; Nüyan led troops to engage him and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: Pu Zezhi, the Song commissioner of Sichuan, attacked Chengdu; Nüyan met him in battle and routed him;

sentences.zh: 進攻雲頂山，守將姚某等以眾相繼來降。

translations.literal: advancing to attack Yunding Mountain, where the garrison commanders Yao and others successively came over with their forces.
translations.idiomatic: then pressed on to Yunding Mountain, where the garrison commanders Yao and others surrendered one after another with their troops.

sentences.zh: 詔以紐鄰為都元帥。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Nüyan supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Nüyan supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 帝由東勝渡河。

translations.literal: The Emperor crossed the river from Dongsheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor forded the river from Dongsheng.

sentences.zh: 遣參知政事劉太平括興元戶口。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Liu Taiping was dispatched to register the households of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Liu Taiping was sent to register the households of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 三月，命洪茶丘率師從劄剌同征高麗。

translations.literal: In the third month Hong Chagiu was ordered to lead troops following Qarachar in the campaign against Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hong Chagiu was ordered to take troops and join Qarachar in the campaign against Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，駐蹕六盤山，諸郡縣守令來覲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he halted at Liupan Mountain; the magistrates of the commanderies and counties came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month he encamped at Liupan Mountain, and the prefectural and county magistrates came to audience.

sentences.zh: 豐州千戶郭燧奏請續簽軍千人修治金州，從之。

translations.literal: Guo Sui, thousand-household commander of Fengzhou, petitioned to conscript another thousand troops to repair Jinzhou; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Sui, thousand-household commander of Fengzhou, asked to conscript another thousand men to repair Jinzhou, and the petition was granted.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍四萬，號十萬，分三道而進：帝由隴州入散關，諸王莫哥由洋州入米倉關，孛裏義萬戶由漁關入沔州。

translations.literal: At this time the army numbered forty thousand but was proclaimed as one hundred thousand, advancing in three columns: the Emperor entered through San Pass from Longzhou; Prince Möge entered through Micang Pass from Yangzhou; and the thousand-household commander Boriy entered through Yu Pass into Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The army then stood at forty thousand but marched under the banner of one hundred thousand, split into three columns: the Emperor entered by San Pass from Longzhou; Prince Möge by Micang Pass from Yangzhou; and the thousand-household commander Boriy by Yu Pass into Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 以明安答兒為太傅，守京兆。

translations.literal: Minggansar was appointed Grand Preceptor to guard Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Minggansar was made Grand Preceptor and left to hold Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 詔征益都行省李亶兵，璮來言：「益都南北要衝，兵不可撤。

translations.literal: An edict summoned the forces of Li Tan, chief of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. Tan came and said, "Yidu is the vital junction between north and south; the troops cannot be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called up the troops of Li Tan, chief of the Yidu Branch Secretariat. Tan came in person and said, "Yidu is the hinge between north and south; the army cannot be pulled away.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " His plea was granted.

sentences.zh: 璮還，擊海州、漣水等處。

translations.literal: Tan returned and attacked Haizhou, Lianshui, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Tan returned and struck Haizhou, Lianshui, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 五月，皇子阿速帶因獵獨騎傷民稼，帝見讓之，遂撻近侍數人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the prince Asudai, while hunting alone on horseback, trampled the people's crops. The Emperor reproached him upon seeing it and had several attendants flogged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince Asudai, hunting alone, rode through the peasants' fields and ruined the crop. When the Emperor saw it he rebuked him and had several attendants whipped.

sentences.zh: 士卒有拔民蔥者，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: Any soldier who pulled up scallions from civilian fields was immediately beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier who so much as pulled an onion from a farmer's plot was beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 由是秋毫莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Henceforth not even the slightest thing dared be touched.
translations.idiomatic: After that not a blade of grass was touched.

sentences.zh: 仍賜所經郡守各有差。

translations.literal: The magistrates of the districts passed through were further rewarded in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates of the districts the army passed through were rewarded in turn, each according to his merit.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，留輜重於六盤山，率兵由寶雞攻重貴山，所至輒平。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he left the baggage train at Liupan Mountain and led troops through Baoji to attack Chongguishan; wherever they went they pacified the land.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he left the baggage at Liupan Mountain and led the army through Baoji against Chongguishan, reducing every place they reached.

sentences.zh: 八月辛丑，璮與宋人戰，殺宋師殆盡。

translations.literal: On xinchou day in the eighth month Tan fought the Song and slaughtered their army nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day in the eighth month Tan met the Song in battle and cut their force nearly to the last man.

sentences.zh: 九月，駐蹕漢中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he halted at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he encamped at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 都元帥紐鄰留密裏火者、劉黑馬等守成都，悉率余兵渡馬湖，禽宋制置使張實，遂遣實招諭苦竹隘，實遁。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Nüyan left Milihuozhe, Liu Heima, and others to guard Chengdu, then led the remaining troops across Mahu Lake, captured the Song commissioner Zhang Shi, and sent Shi to summon Kuzhu Pass to surrender; Shi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Nüyan left Milihuozhe, Liu Heima, and others to hold Chengdu, then crossed Mahu Lake with the rest of his force, captured the Song commissioner Zhang Shi, and sent him to call on Kuzhu Pass to surrender; Shi fled.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬午，帝次寶峰。

translations.literal: On rewu day in the tenth month of winter the Emperor halted at Baofeng.
translations.idiomatic: On rewu day in the tenth winter month the Emperor encamped at Baofeng.

sentences.zh: 癸未，如利州，觀其城池並非深固，以汪田哥能守，蜀不敢犯，賜卮酒獎諭之。

translations.literal: On guiwei day he went to Lizhou. Seeing that its walls were not especially deep or strong, yet because Wang Tiange had held them ably and Shu had not dared attack, he granted a cup of wine in commendation.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day he entered Lizhou. The walls were neither deep nor strong, but Wang Tiange had held them so well that Shu had never dared strike; the Emperor raised a cup of wine in praise.

sentences.zh: 帝渡嘉陵江，至白水江，命田哥造浮梁以濟，梁成，賜田哥等金帛有差。

translations.literal: The Emperor crossed the Jialing River to the Baishui River, ordered Tiange to build a pontoon bridge for the crossing; when it was finished, he granted Tiange and the others gold and silk in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor crossed the Jialing to the Baishui and ordered Tiange to build a pontoon bridge. When it was ready he rewarded Tiange and his men with gold and silk in graded gifts.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕劍門。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor encamped at Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 戊子，攻苦竹隘，裨將趙仲竊獻東南門，師入，與其守將楊立戰，敗之，殺立，眾皆奔潰。

translations.literal: On wuzi day they attacked Kuzhu Pass. Vice-commander Zhao Zhong secretly opened the southeast gate; the army entered, fought the garrison commander Yang Li, defeated him, killed Li, and the troops all fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day they assaulted Kuzhu Pass. Vice-commander Zhao Zhong opened the southeast gate from within; the army poured in, fought the garrison commander Yang Li, broke him, and killed him, and the defenders fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 詔毋犯趙仲家屬，仍賜仲衣帽，徙于隆慶。

translations.literal: An edict forbade harming Zhao Zhong's family; Zhong was further granted hat and robes and transferred to Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict protected Zhao Zhong's household from reprisal, granted him hat and robes, and moved him to Longqing.

sentences.zh: 己亥，獲張實，支解之。

translations.literal: On jihai day Zhang Shi was captured and dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day Zhang Shi was taken and torn limb from limb.

sentences.zh: 賜田哥玉帶及犒賞士卒，留精兵五百守之。

translations.literal: Tiange was granted a jade belt and the troops were rewarded; five hundred picked soldiers were left to garrison the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tiange received a jade belt and the troops were given bounty; five hundred picked men were left to hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 遣使招諭龍州。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to summon Longzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were dispatched to call on Longzhou to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝至高峰。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Gaofeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor advanced to Gaofeng.

sentences.zh: 庚子，圍長寧山，守將王佐、裨將徐昕等率兵出戰，敗之。

translations.literal: On gengzi day they besieged Changning Mountain; garrison commander Wang Zuo and vice-commander Xu Xin led troops out to fight and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day they invested Changning Mountain; garrison commander Wang Zuo and vice-commander Xu Xin sallied out and were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 十一月己酉，帝督軍先攻鵝頂堡。

translations.literal: On yiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor personally directed the army, first attacking Eding Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the eleventh month the Emperor took command in person and opened the assault on Eding Fort.

sentences.zh: 壬子，力戰於望喜門。

translations.literal: On renzi day they fought fiercely at Wangxi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day they fought hard at Wangxi Gate.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，宋知縣王仲由鵝頂堡出降。

translations.literal: At dusk Song magistrate Wang Zhong came out from Eding Fort to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the Song magistrate Wang Zhong came down from Eding Fort to surrender.

sentences.zh: 是夜破其城，王佐死焉。

translations.literal: That night the city was taken; Wang Zuo died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: That night the city fell; Wang Zuo died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，誅佐之子及徐昕等四十餘人。

translations.literal: On guichou day Zuo's sons and Xu Xin and more than forty others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day Zuo's sons, Xu Xin, and more than forty others were put to death.

sentences.zh: 以彭天祥為達魯花赤治其事，王仲副之。

translations.literal: Peng Tianxiang was appointed darughachi to administer the place, with Wang Zhong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Tianxiang was made darughachi to govern the district, with Wang Zhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，進攻大獲山，守將楊大淵降，命大淵為四川侍郎，仍以其兵從。

translations.literal: On bingchen day they advanced to attack Daguo Mountain; garrison commander Yang Dayuan submitted and was appointed Vice Minister of Sichuan, and his troops followed with the army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day they pressed the attack on Daguo Mountain; garrison commander Yang Dayuan came over, was named Vice Minister of Sichuan, and marched on with his men.

sentences.zh: 庚午，次和溪口，遣驍騎略青居山。

translations.literal: On gengwu day they halted at Hexikou and sent bold cavalry to raid Qingju Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day they halted at Hexikou and sent swift cavalry to sweep Qingju Mountain.

sentences.zh: 是月，龍州王知府降。

translations.literal: That month the Wang prefect of Longzhou submitted.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Wang family prefect of Longzhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 諸王莫哥都攻禮義山不克，諸王塔察兒略地至江而還，並會於行在所。

translations.literal: Prince Mögedü attacked Liyi Mountain but could not take it; Prince Tachar raided as far as the river and returned; both joined the Emperor at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mögedü assaulted Liyi Mountain without success; Prince Tachar raided to the river and turned back; both rejoined the Emperor at the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 命忽必烈統諸路蒙古、漢軍伐宋。

translations.literal: Kublai was ordered to command the Mongol and Han armies of all circuits in the campaign against the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was ordered to take command of the Mongol and Han armies of every circuit for the war against the Song.

sentences.zh: 十二月壬午，楊大淵率所部兵與汪田哥分擊相如等縣。

translations.literal: On rewu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan led his troops with Wang Tiange to strike Xiangru and other counties separately.
translations.idiomatic: On rewu day in the twelfth month Yang Dayuan and Wang Tiange split their forces to strike Xiangru and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 都元帥紐鄰攻簡州，以宋降將張威率眾為先鋒。

translations.literal: Supreme commander Nüyan attacked Jianzhou, with the Song surrendered general Zhang Wei leading the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme commander Nüyan invested Jianzhou, with the Song turncoat Zhang Wei at the head of the van.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，帝次於運山。

translations.literal: On yiyou day the Emperor halted at Yunshan.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day the Emperor encamped at Yunshan.

sentences.zh: 大 淵遣人招降其守將張大悅，仍以大悅為元帥。

translations.literal: Dayuan sent men to summon the garrison commander Zhang Dayue to submit, and appointed Dayue commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan sent envoys to win over the garrison commander Zhang Dayue and made Dayue commander-in-chief once he submitted.

sentences.zh: 師至青居山，裨將劉淵等殺都統段元鑒降。

translations.literal: The army reached Qingju Mountain; the assistant general Liu Yuan and others killed the commander Duan Yuanjian and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Qingju Mountain, where the assistant commander Liu Yuan and his officers killed the garrison commander Duan Yuanjian and submitted.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，遣使招諭未附。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, envoys were sent to summon and instruct those not yet submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day, envoys were dispatched to call in those who had not yet submitted.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，隆州守縣降。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, the district magistrate defending Long Prefecture surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day, the magistrate holding Long Prefecture surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己亥，大良山守將蒲元圭降。

translations.literal: On jihai day, the defending general Pu Yuangui of Daliang Mountain surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, Pu Yuangui, who held Daliang Mountain, came over.

sentences.zh: 詔諸軍毋俘掠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all armies not to take captives or plunder.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade the armies to loot or take prisoners.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，攻雅州，拔之。

translations.literal: On guimao day, they attacked Ya Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day they stormed Ya Prefecture and captured it.

sentences.zh: 石泉守將趙順降。

translations.literal: The defending general Zhao Shun of Shiquan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shun, the garrison commander at Shiquan, submitted.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，遣宋人晉國寶招諭合州守將王堅，堅辭之，國寶遂歸。

translations.literal: On jiachen day, the Song man Jin Guobao was sent to summon and instruct Wang Jian, the defending general of He Prefecture; Wang Jian declined, and Guobao then returned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day the Emperor sent the Song defector Jin Guobao to treat with Wang Jian, He Prefecture's commander; Wang Jian refused, and Guobao turned back.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皇子辨都薨于吉河之南。

translations.literal: That year, the prince Bian Du died south of the Ji River.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Bian Du died on the south bank of the Ji River.

sentences.zh: 九年己未春正月乙巳朔，駐蹕重貴山北，置酒大會，因問諸王、駙馬、百官曰：「今在宋境，夏暑且至，汝等其謂可居否乎？

translations.literal: In the ninth year, jiwei, spring, first month, on yisi day (new moon), the Emperor halted north of Zhongguishan, set out wine at a great assembly, and asked the princes, imperial sons-in-law, and officials: "We are now in Song territory; the summer heat is about to come — do you think we can remain here?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (jiwei), on the new moon of the first spring month, the Emperor encamped north of Zhongguishan and held a great feast. He asked his princes, sons-in-law, and ministers, "We are deep in Song territory, and the summer heat is coming — can we endure it here?

sentences.zh: 」劄剌亦兒部人脫歡曰：「南土瘴癘，上宜北還，所獲人民，委吏治之便。

translations.literal: " Toqur of the Jadaran tribe said, "The southern lands are malarial; Your Majesty should return north. It would be best to leave the people we have taken to be administered by officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Toqur of the Jadaran tribe replied, "These southern lands breed pestilence. Your Majesty should withdraw north and leave the people we have taken to be governed by appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 」阿兒剌部人八里赤曰：「脫歡怯，臣願往居焉。

translations.literal: " Baraq of the Arlat tribe said, "Toqur is faint-hearted. Your servant is willing to remain and dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: " Baraq of the Arlat tribe answered, "Toqur lacks nerve. Your servant will gladly stay and hold these lands.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was pleased by this.

sentences.zh: 戊申，晉國寶歸次峽口，王堅追還殺之。

translations.literal: On wushen day, Jin Guobao, on his return, halted at Xiakou; Wang Jian pursued, brought him back, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day Guobao was making his way back when he halted at the gorge mouth; Wang Jian overtook him, hauled him back, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 諸王莫哥都復攻渠州禮義山，曳剌禿魯雄攻巴州平梁山。

translations.literal: Prince Mogedu again attacked Liyi Mountain in Qu Prefecture; Yelü Chulu Xiong attacked Pingliang Mountain in Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mogedu renewed the assault on Liyi Mountain in Qu Prefecture, while Yelü Chulu Xiong attacked Pingliang Mountain in Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，大淵請攻合州，俘男女八萬餘。

translations.literal: On dingmao day, Dayuan requested to attack He Prefecture and took more than eighty thousand men and women captive.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Yang Dayuan asked leave to assault He Prefecture and brought in more than eighty thousand captives, men and women together.

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，帝悉率諸兵渡雞爪灘，至石子山。

translations.literal: In the second month, on bingzi day, the Emperor led all troops across Jizhuo Beach to Shizi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on bingzi day, the Emperor led the full host across Chicken-claw Beach to Stone Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，督諸軍戰城下。

translations.literal: On dingchou day, he supervised the armies fighting below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he drove his armies to battle beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，攻一字城。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, they attacked Yizi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day they assaulted the One-character Fort.

sentences.zh: 癸未，攻鎮西門。

translations.literal: On guiwei day, they attacked the Western Gate of the Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day they struck the Western Gate bastion.

sentences.zh: 三月，攻東新門、奇勝門、鎮西門小堡。

translations.literal: In the third month, they attacked the Eastern New Gate, the Qisheng Gate, and the small fort at the Western Gate bastion.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month they pressed the Eastern New Gate, the Gate of Strange Victories, and the outer works of the Western Gate.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙子，大雷雨凡二十日。

translations.literal: In the fourth summer month, on bingzi day, great thunder and rain lasted twenty days altogether.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month, on bingzi day, torrential storms rolled on for twenty days.

sentences.zh: 乙未，攻護國門。

translations.literal: On yiwei day, they attacked the Gate of Guarding the State.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day they stormed the Gate of Guarding the State.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，夜登外城，殺宋兵甚眾。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, at night they scaled the outer wall and killed a great many Song soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day, under cover of night, they climbed the outer wall and cut down large numbers of Song defenders.

sentences.zh: 五月，屢攻不克。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, repeated attacks failed to take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Through the fifth month they battered the fortress again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，汪田哥復選兵夜登外城馬軍寨，殺寨主及守城者。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange again selected troops, and at night scaled the outer-wall Cavalry Fort, killing the fort commander and the defenders.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingsi day, Wang Tiange handpicked a force that climbed the cavalry redoubt on the outer wall by night and killed its commander and the men holding it.

sentences.zh: 王堅率兵來戰。

translations.literal: Wang Jian led troops to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian came out to fight.

sentences.zh: 遲明，遇雨，梯折，後軍不克進而止。

translations.literal: At dawn, rain fell; the siege ladders broke, and the rear army could not advance, so they halted.
translations.idiomatic: Near daybreak rain swept in; the ladders snapped, the rear columns could not follow, and the assault was called off.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝不豫。

translations.literal: That month, the Emperor fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Emperor took ill.

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛亥，留精兵三千守之，余悉攻重慶。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinhai day, three thousand picked troops were left to hold the place, and the rest all attacked Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh autumn month, on xinhai day, he left three thousand elite troops to hold the siege and marched the rest against Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝崩於釣魚山，壽五十有二，在位九年。

translations.literal: On guihai day, the Emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain; he was fifty-two years old and had reigned nine years.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day the Emperor died at Diaoyu Mountain. He was fifty-two and had ruled nine years.

sentences.zh: 追諡桓肅皇帝，廟號憲宗。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Huansu; his temple name was Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was styled Emperor Huansu; his temple name was Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 帝剛明雄毅，沉斷而寡言，不樂燕飲，不好侈靡，雖后妃不許之過制。

translations.literal: The Emperor was resolute, bright, fierce, and steadfast; he was deep in judgment and sparing of speech; he took no pleasure in feasting and drinking, and did not love extravagance — not even the consorts were permitted to exceed proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was hard-minded and quick to decide, fierce in bearing and sparing of speech. He took no pleasure in revelry or display, and would not even let his consorts exceed the bounds of custom.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗朝，群臣擅權，政出多門。

translations.literal: In the beginning, during Taizong's reign, ministers wielded power on their own authority, and government issued from many gates.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's day ministers had seized power for themselves, and policy issued from many hands.

sentences.zh: 至是，凡有詔旨，帝必親起草，更易數四，然後行之。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever there were edicts and orders, the Emperor personally drafted them, revising them three or four times before issuing them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth he drafted every edict himself, revising each four times over before it went out.

sentences.zh: 御群臣甚嚴，嘗諭旨曰：「爾輩若得朕獎諭之言，即志氣驕逸，志氣驕逸，而災禍有不隨至者乎？

translations.literal: In governing his ministers he was very strict; he once instructed them: "If you obtain words of commendation from me, you at once grow proud and dissolute in spirit; when the spirit turns proud and dissolute, can disaster fail to follow?
translations.idiomatic: He governed his court with stern discipline and once warned them, "Let me once praise you, and your spirits swell with pride; when pride swells, can ruin be far behind?

sentences.zh: 爾輩其戒之。

translations.literal: You must guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Guard yourselves against it.

sentences.zh: 」性喜畋獵，自謂遵祖宗之法，不蹈襲他國所為。

translations.literal: " He loved hunting by nature and held that he was following the ways of his forebears, not treading in the customs of other states.
translations.idiomatic: " Hunting was his passion; he held that in this he followed ancestral custom, not the habits of other realms.

sentences.zh: 然酷信巫覡卜筮之術，凡行事必謹叩之，殆無虛日，終不自厭也。

translations.literal: Yet he deeply believed in the arts of shamans and divination; in all undertakings he scrupulously consulted them — scarcely a day passed without this — and he never wearied of it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he trusted shamans and oracles utterly; before any undertaking he consulted them, almost without a day's exception, and never seemed to grow weary of the practice.
